title: Invertible-order cases for a prime-annihilated sheaf
statement: Let k be a field, Λ a commutative ring, X a scheme and r a prime. For an etale sheaf F of Λ-modules with r id_F = 0, if r is a unit in Γ(Spec k, top), F has invertible-order torsion relative to Spec k. If r is not a unit there, invertible-order torsion forces F to be zero. The coefficient condition is the one of [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions].

source.place: Tag 0GJA (lemma-restrict-to-open), proof: the finite stalk product, five-term exact sequence, and remarks (a) and (b)

proof.text: Apply the additive stalk functors to the annihilation equality. If r is a unit, it is a common positive invertible annihilator, as required by the coefficient condition.
Use ΓSpecIso to pass to k. If r is not a unit, r is zero in k. An integer n invertible in k is not divisible by r. The stalk is killed by both r and n, and nsmul_eq_zero_iff_of_coprime makes it zero.
Use sheafHom_ext_of_sheafFiber_map_algClosurePoint and IsZero.iff_id_eq_zero to conclude that F is zero.
